title: Two different people are linked as one
hazard: A new registration or an import is auto-linked to another person's record
cause: Matcher false positive: similar names and birth dates, shared address, a typo that makes two NHS numbers collide, twins
effect: Clinician sees, and writes to, another person's identity record; later clinical content would be attributed to the wrong person
controls: Twins never AutoLink; two different valid NHS numbers are NonMatch; a missing given name, family name or birth date blocks AutoLink; absent evidence is None not zero; review band routes to a person; duplicate check at registration needs a written override reason; compare is symmetric, so the order in which two records are compared never changes the decision (given names of equal length are averaged both ways and the lower kept); a repeated-digit NHS number (0000000000 and the like) is a placeholder, invalid, and never decides a link; a shared NHS number with both given and family names disagreeing goes to Review; a shared NHS number with two different full birth dates always goes to Review, however close the dates; birth-date typo credit only for a one-digit slip or an adjacent swap (a parent and child sharing a birthday score 0), and an impossible date is absent; a given name that folds to nothing (a dash, spaces) is absent, not a disagreement; the service uses matcher 0.4.0 (published 2026-10-26), which carries all of these controls and CQ-37, and refuses a placeholder NHS number at registration; since 0.3.0 (CQ-19) a given name on one record that nothing on the other matches (John against John Paul) blocks AutoLink, and a family name of several parts is compared part by part so Smith-Jones does not match Smithson; a name is also compared transliterated (Müller as Mueller, José as Jose), taking the better score, which can raise a similarity but never lowers one and leaves other scripts alone; given and family names keyed into each other's boxes (Taylor Morgan against Morgan Taylor) are scored at 0.9 of their similarity and blocked from AutoLink with a stated conflict, so they go to Review; a combining mark (virama, vowel sign) stays with its letter, so an Indic or Persian name is one word, not several fragments; phone numbers are compared in E.164 form (07700 900123 and +44 7700 900123 are one number) and a number under 7 digits is absent, not a match; a shared postcode, or a shared phone with no shared email, counts at half weight as household evidence, so relatives at one address are not lifted toward a link; a nickname and its formal name (Bill, William) score 0.8, under the given-name auto-link minimum, so they reach Review and never link on the name alone; a pair the spelling scores as unrelated but whose family and first given name sound alike (Soundex), with the same birth date, goes to Review with a stated conflict, the score unchanged; a placeholder name (Unknown, Unidentified, Anonymous, UNK-nnn) is absent evidence, so two unidentified patients never match each other and an unidentified patient never auto-links to a real record; the registration and compare pages show each reason a link cannot be automatic from its stable code in the page's language, falling back to the matcher's English text for a code they do not know (CQ-38; the nine-locale wording is machine-written and unreviewed); (matcher 0.4.0, CQ-37) a shared valid NHS number with a given name, family name or birth date absent on either record goes to Review, not AutoLink
residual: Thresholds (auto_link 0.92, review 0.75) are unvalidated guesses with no real-data evaluation; there is no merge yet (ID-5) so no auto-link is performed by the service. Gap found 2026-10-23 (CQ-30, CQ-37): a shared valid NHS number linked automatically even with no names or birth date present. Decided 2026-10-25 (maintainer; the Clinical Safety Officer has not reviewed it): a missing given name, family name or birth date now sends a shared-number pair to Review, in matcher 0.4.0 (tests/properties.rs::a_shared_nhs_number_alone_goes_to_review), published 2026-10-26 and used by the service. Added 2026-10-25: no clinician has retested the CQ-19 rules (part-by-part family names, nicknames, phonetic Review, swap) against the service now that it runs 0.4.0, and the thresholds were not re-evaluated; the translated reasons are machine-written and no speaker has reviewed them

title: A duplicate record is created
hazard: A person is registered again although a record exists
cause: Candidate search only finds records sharing a family name, a birth date or an identifier; a re-registration with all three different (name change, wrong birth date) is not a candidate; two registrations of one person at the same moment (two clerks, a clerk and the HL7 feed, two feed connections) each passing the check before the other was stored
effect: Split history: information entered on one record is missing on the other; allergies or alerts not seen
controls: Duplicate check at registration with side-by-side view and override reason; search by name, birth date and identifier; the duplicate check, the insert and the audit row run in one transaction under a registration lock, for registration by a person and by the HL7 feed alike, so concurrent registrations of one person cannot both pass; candidates are ranked by evidence (a shared identifier, then family name and birth date together) before the 200 limit, and a cut list is reported; the register form ignores a second click while one request is in flight (CQ-33), so a double click cannot post the same registration twice
residual: Documented blind spot (nothing in common is not a candidate); no phonetic search; no merge or unmerge to repair a split (ID-5); when more than 200 records share a birth date or family name only the 200 strongest are compared: one sharing an identifier, or the family name and birth date, always is, but one sharing only a name or only a birth date (a mistyped birth date, say) can be cut; the registration page then says so, while an HL7 create only records it in the audit row

title: An invalid or mistyped NHS number is accepted
hazard: An identifier is stored that does not belong to the person
cause: Typing error that still passes, or an invalid number entered
effect: Wrong-patient lookup or failed lookup on an external system
controls: Modulus-11 check on every NHS number at create and update; HL7 and FHIR inputs go through the same validation
residual: A valid-looking wrong number still passes; no PDS (national service) trace exists

title: An edit overwrites a newer edit
hazard: Two people change the same record and one change is lost
cause: Concurrent edit without a version check
effect: Correct demographics replaced by stale ones
controls: Append-only versions with optimistic expected_version (409 on stale, one winner in a race); FHIR update requires If-Match (428/412)
residual: UI shows the conflict but does not merge field by field

title: A record is shown to someone not entitled
hazard: A user reads identity data they should not
cause: Error in the unreviewed role and purpose permission table; a route missing from the table; a relationship wrongly recorded
effect: Confidentiality breach; loss of trust; legal exposure
controls: Route gate refuses any route not in the table (census test); record-level decision on role, relationship, purpose and consent; every read audited; refusals audited
residual: The permission table is a first draft and has not been reviewed by a clinical safety officer or a privacy officer; the service does not verify that a token sub is the patient it is linked to

title: A patient's consent refusal is ignored
hazard: A record is disclosed after the patient refused
cause: Consent not applied on some path (search, duplicate check, FHIR, a future export)
effect: Breach of the patient's choice; breach of law for Part 2 data
controls: Consent applied on identity read, search (hidden results dropped, counted only in the audit row) and the duplicate check; a deny always wins; an unreadable provision denies; FHIR endpoints run the same handlers
residual: No bulk export, clinical content or UI for consent exists yet; each new read path must be checked against this hazard; the national data opt-out service is local only

title: Sensitive information is shown unmasked
hazard: Substance-use, HIV, psychiatric or restricted data appears to staff without a need
cause: Security labels not enforced when clinical content arrives
effect: Harm to the patient (discrimination, safety); breach of 42 CFR Part 2 style rules
controls: The policy engine decides on labels and a general permit never unmasks SUD; there is no clinical content yet
residual: Masking (SE-4) is not built; this hazard is latent until clinical content exists and must be re-assessed then

title: A clinician cannot see a record in an emergency
hazard: Care is delayed because access is refused
cause: A clinician has no care relationship with a patient in an emergency; break-the-glass was not built (now built, see H-024)
effect: Delayed treatment
controls: Break-the-glass (SE-3): a treating clinician with no care relationship is refused with an offer, gives a reason and acknowledges, and reads clinical content for 4 hours; purpose emergency is still not offered in the staff picker
residual: Care can still be delayed by the extra steps (a reason, a tick) and by a patient's refusal of consent, which break-the-glass deliberately does not lift; only reads of clinical content are opened (a clinician still cannot record without a relationship); the screens are English only; ratings are unreviewed

title: The audit trail is altered or truncated unnoticed
hazard: Access is hidden or evidence is lost
cause: Someone with database access edits or deletes audit rows, or the chain is unkeyed
effect: Misuse cannot be shown; patients are told a false access history
controls: Append-only table with triggers; hash chain, keyed MAC when EPR_INTEGRITY_MAC_KEY is set; verify endpoint; a head checkpoint detects removed newest rows; an unheld key is reported as a key problem not tampering
residual: The key is optional (unkeyed chain by default); nothing stores the head checkpoint for the operator; removed newest rows are undetected without one

title: An access happens without an audit row
hazard: An access is not recorded
cause: Audit write fails and the request still answers; a path forgets to audit
effect: Misuse cannot be shown
controls: Handlers audit before the data leaves and answer 500 if the row cannot be written; patient, consent and relationship writes and their audit row are one transaction, so a write that cannot be audited does not happen; refusals are audited
residual: A refusal row that cannot be written is logged only; 401, 400 and 422 responses are not audited; reads, refusals and the verify and search rows are audited in their own transactions

title: A relationship wrongly gives access
hazard: A person is linked as the patient, a proxy or care team of someone they are not
cause: Wrong subject recorded by an administrator; a stale link not ended
effect: Disclosure to the wrong person, including through the patient's own view
controls: Only clinical-admin can record relationships; ending is a new version; every change is audited; the patient's access log shows who looked; a proxy reads only the scopes its terms list and only until its expiry, and a proxy without terms reads nothing (PA-5)
residual: No second person approves a link; no check that the subject is who the administrator says; the proxy scopes and the five-year limit are guesses no clinician has reviewed; no rule yet for a child who becomes able to decide for themself (adolescent confidentiality)

title: Data from another system is stored wrongly
hazard: An HL7 or FHIR message becomes the wrong identity record
cause: A misparsed date or sex, a dropped element, an identifier given no system
effect: Wrong demographics under a right id, or an unusable record
controls: FHIR input with elements the record cannot hold is refused (422); unreadable HL7 date or sex is left blank with a warning; identifiers without an authority are skipped with a warning; HL7 AE/AR acknowledgements
residual: No conformance run; HL7 has no listener yet; HL7 reads MSH and PID only

title: The patient's access log misleads
hazard: The patient is told something false about who looked
cause: Roles are what the token said; older rows have no role; refused attempts shown as access
effect: Wrong belief that a record was or was not seen
controls: Entries say staff with the recorded role and organisation, never a name; refusals are labelled as refused; older entries say only staff
residual: Roles are not checked against a directory; no filter or date range

title: A translated screen is wrong
hazard: A clinician or patient misreads an instruction
cause: Machine-written translations used in the interface
effect: Misunderstanding of a warning or a choice
controls: Translations are marked machine-written until a speaker reviews them; the default English is the reference
residual: No translation has been reviewed by a speaker

title: The system is used for real care although it is not ready
hazard: A site relies on a scaffold
cause: Overstated documentation or a deployment ignoring the warnings
effect: Any of the above, without safeguards
controls: Every README and AGENTS.md says not for clinical use; no clinical content exists; nothing claims certification or compliance
residual: No release gate stops a deployment; the clinical safety officer is not named (OQ-2)

title: The patient banner misleads
hazard: A clinician acts on the wrong person, age or allergy status shown in the banner
cause: Banner built from unsaved form input; a wrong or approximate age; an empty allergy line read as no allergies; a stale view after another user's edit; the previous patient's banner or allergies left on screen, or a late answer for them shown, after moving to another patient
effect: Treatment for the wrong person, or an allergy missed because it was read as absent
controls: The banner renders only the record as stored, never the form being edited; age is whole years or months from a full date, marked about for a partial date, and absent rather than guessed for an unreadable or future date; allergies always read Not recorded in this system and that this does not mean there are none; a record with little on it says what is missing; the version is shown beside the form and a stale save is refused; on moving to another patient the page clears the previous patient's record, allergies, form, photo and emergency-access notice at once, and every answer (record, allergies, look, save, photo) is dropped unless it is for the patient now on screen and is the latest asked for; the patient page shows when the record was last read and, if the latest background look failed or none succeeded for 2.5 minutes, an alert that it may not be current (the record stays on screen); the age is counted on the site's calendar day (the service's EPR_SITE_TIME_ZONE, an IANA name checked at start-up, UTC when unset), so every reader at a site sees the same age and it changes at the site's midnight, not UTC's; the no known allergies" statement's time is shown on the site's clock with the UTC time beside it (2026-10-26)"
residual: The banner does not refresh when someone else edits while it is open (it reloads only on a conflict); no photo exists; the allergy line is a placeholder until allergies are recorded (RC-5) and must then be revisited; ages near midnight use UTC dates. The data-age notice is on the patient page only (not my-record, lists or the compare page); the 2.5-minute limit is a guess; it was tested with a stubbed API, not a real outage. Added 2026-10-25: the site zone is one per service, so a service covering sites in different zones counts every age on one zone's day; an older API that sends no zone leaves the UI on UTC; the setting is not validated against where the patient is; an older API that sends no zone leaves these times in UTC (still labelled UTC); no clinician has reviewed the rule

title: A patient photo is wrong or hostile
hazard: The banner shows another person's face, or an uploaded file harms a viewer
cause: A photo uploaded to the wrong record; an outdated photo; a file that is not an image (script in an SVG, a polyglot); a photo kept in a shared cache
effect: A clinician trusts the face and treats the wrong person; or the viewer's browser runs attacker content
controls: Only PNG and JPEG are stored, decided from the file bytes and not the claimed type, at most 512 KiB, never decoded or resized by the server; served nosniff with a sandboxing CSP and no-store; the photo is identity data under the same role, relationship, purpose and consent rules and every read and write is audited (the write in one transaction with its audit row); uploads carry the version last seen so a stale write is refused; removing a photo is a new version and the history stays; the banner always shows the photo of the stored current version; the photo is shown beside the name, birth date and NHS number so a mismatch is visible
residual: Nothing checks that the photo is of this patient or even of a face; no virus or content scan; an image with hostile metadata is stored as is (never parsed here, but a downstream viewer may parse it); the client must not be trusted to size or type-check; old photo versions stay in backups

title: Allergy information is missing, stale or read as none
hazard: A clinician gives or prescribes something the patient reacts to, because the banner or list did not warn
cause: Allergies never recorded; a stated no-known-allergies that is out of date; an allergy ended or retracted wrongly; the viewing role or relationship is refused; the call fails; the criticality is not stated
effect: Anaphylaxis or other serious harm
controls: Every state where the system does not know says so in words and adds that this does not mean there are none (not recorded, not shown to you, could not be loaded); none known is only shown when a named clinician stated it at a time and nothing has been recorded since, and it cannot be stated while an active allergy exists; an active allergy always outranks a statement; high-criticality allergies lead the list and are marked; a risk that was not stated is not shown as low; the banner and the list share one answer; entered in error is final and only a clinician may set it; every version, author and reason is kept and nothing is deleted
residual: Only a thin allergy record exists: no drug-class or cross-reactivity (OR-6), no coded medicines list, no alert at prescribing, no second-person check, no reconciliation with other systems; the SNOMED check is shape-only; substances are free text so the same allergy can be recorded twice in different words; the banner reloads once a minute so a change is not instant

title: An allergy is ended or retracted wrongly
hazard: A real allergy stops being shown
cause: Marking an allergy no longer applies or entered in error by mistake, by the wrong person, or on the wrong patient
effect: The warning disappears and the patient is exposed
controls: Ending is a new version and entered in error is a separate permission held by clinicians, not nurses; both need the version last seen; the whole history with author and reason stays and is visible to an auditor; every change is audited with its patient in one transaction; an ended allergy still counts as a record so none known is not claimed
residual: No confirmation step in the page; no alert to the patient or a pharmacist when an allergy is ended; reading the history of an allergy has no screen yet (only the audit trail and the database)

title: Two different people are merged, or a merge hides information
hazard: One person's record is treated as another's after a merge, or something recorded against one is lost from view
cause: An administrator merges records of different people; a merge of look-alike records; allergies or consent not following the merge; an old record still edited
effect: Treatment of one person on another's allergies and history; a consent refusal ignored; information lost
controls: A merge is a link, never a rewrite: nothing is deleted or moved, so unmerging restores both records exactly (checked by a property test against a model); only the clinical-admin role may merge, with a required reason; the matcher must not call the pair a non-match, and two different verified NHS numbers always refuse; the surviving record shows the merged-in allergies (each still naming the record it was made on) and a consent refusal on either record applies to both; the old record is read-only, says where it went in its banner, search and the duplicate check; a care relationship does not carry over; merges are serialised and cannot cycle; every merge and unmerge is audited in one transaction with the matcher verdict
residual: The matcher threshold is an unvalidated guess; nothing asks a second person to confirm a merge; there is no review queue of uncertain pairs (a person has to find them); only allergies, consent and identity follow a merge today, and every new kind of clinical content must be taught to follow it or it will silently stay on the old record; photos and relationships do not follow; the surviving record's no-known-allergies statement is not combined with the old record's

title: An HL7 feed writes the wrong demographics, or the port is open to anyone
hazard: A patient record is created or changed by a message that should not have been applied
cause: A misconfigured or hostile sender; a feed bound beyond the machine; a mis-mapped field; a message for the wrong person; MLLP has no authentication
effect: Wrong identity data under a right patient, a duplicate record, or an attacker rewriting names
controls: The listener is off unless EPR_MLLP_BIND is set, refuses a non-loopback address without an explicit allow, and refuses to start on any bad setting; the audit agent is configured and the peer address recorded, nothing the sender claims is trusted; the feed's role may only create and update identity (checked by the policy engine, never read or export); matching is on identifiers and an ambiguous match is refused; a possible duplicate is refused rather than created; an update never blanks a field, and never changes a birth date or NHS number; a repeat writes nothing; the write and its audit row are one transaction; size, connection and idle limits; unreadable streams close; a refused message is kept in a work queue (feed_refusals) that a clinical administrator reads and closes with an outcome and a reason, each step audited
residual: No authentication or encryption on MLLP itself; the deployer must provide a TLS terminator or private network; the work queue has a screen but no alert and no age limit, so a refusal nobody looks at waits and the sender may have stopped holding the message; the integrator role can now also create and update identity over the REST API; a wrong name from a trusted feed is applied (the first name is replaced); an A08 for a record that was merged away is treated as a new patient and then refused as a possible duplicate; no conformance testing with a real sender

title: Allergy data read through FHIR is taken to mean there are none
hazard: An outside system reads an empty or partial AllergyIntolerance result as "no allergies" and a clinician acts on it
cause: An empty or inactive-only search result; a consumer ignoring the OperationOutcome entry; a 403 or consent refusal shown as an empty list; an allergy entered in error left out; verification status and type not recorded; allergy under the surviving record after a merge
effect: A drug or food given to a person with an allergy the other system did not show
controls: An empty result always carries an OperationOutcome saying it does not mean there are none; only a standing clinician statement is exported as SNOMED 716186003 no known allergy; a refusal is an error with the same sentence, never an empty bundle; unstated criticality is omitted, never low; verificationStatus and type are omitted, not guessed; the result is checked against the typed R4 model; the same handler applies the gate, care relationship, purpose, consent and audit as the REST route
residual: No UK Core or US Core profile validation and no HAPI run; a consumer can still ignore the outcome entry; no read by id and no write; entered-in-error allergies are not exported so a consumer cannot reconcile them; ratings are unreviewed

title: A refused HL7 message is never seen, or its text is seen by the wrong person
hazard: A patient's registration or correction sent by another system is refused and then lost, or the stored message is read by someone who should not see it
cause: Nobody works the queue; the queue has no screen or alert; a refusal closed as dismissed in error; the stored message is patient data for a person who may not be on record
effect: Wrong or missing demographics persist; a clinician works from a record that never received an update; a disclosure of a message text
controls: Each refusal is stored as received in append-only tables and stays until a person closes it once, with an outcome and a reason, and the closing is audited; only the clinical administrator role may read or close the queue (policy FeedQueue); a listing carries no message text and each read of a message is audited by id, never by content; the refusal is also in the audit trail; an administrator screen (/admin/feed) lists the open entries, shows a message on request and closes it with an outcome and a required reason; the navigation shows how many are waiting on the admin pages
residual: The count shows only on the admin pages (an administrator who never opens one never sees it), with no alert, no count on the home page and no age limit, so an unseen refusal is silent; messages are stored as plain text in the database like other patient data; "handled" is the closer's word and is not checked against the record; a temporary failure is not queued; ratings are unreviewed

title: Break-the-glass is used without need, or never reviewed
hazard: A clinician opens a patient's record without a clinical reason, or a misuse goes unnoticed
cause: A reason typed to get past the prompt; a grant used for curiosity; nobody reviews the queue; there is no real-time notification to a privacy officer; a reviewer who is a friend of the clinician
effect: A patient's confidential information is disclosed to someone with no care duty; the misuse is found late or never
controls: A mandatory reason and acknowledgement; a fixed 4-hour grant that asking again does not extend; only treating roles; the grant lifts only the missing care relationship for reads of clinical content (not writes, not a patient's refusal of consent, not a label); every audit row of the access is flagged break-glass and names the grant; the patient sees that it happened in their access log; every grant waits in an unreviewed queue for the auditor role, once, with a note, and not by the person who opened it; append-only tables; the grant's start and expiry are shown on the site's clock with the UTC time beside it (2026-10-26), so staff at a site read the same expiry
residual: No real-time notification (nothing can send one); no count or alert for the review queue, so it is silent until the auditor opens the page; the reason is free text and is not checked; nothing detects patterns such as one clinician opening many grants; a grant lasts 4 hours with no way to end it early; sensitive-record masking (SE-4) is not built so a grant shows everything the role may read; ratings are unreviewed

title: A session stays open on an unattended workstation, or ends while a clinician is working
hazard: Someone else reads or writes under a clinician's sign-in, or a clinician loses unsaved work when signed out
cause: A page that polls in the background kept the session alive indefinitely (fixed); a sign-out for inactivity with no warning; a warning not seen; a clinician typing a long entry without saving
effect: A disclosure, or an entry made under the wrong person's name; or an entry lost and not re-entered
controls: Background looks (the patient page's minute poll of the record and allergies) are marked and never count as activity, in the hook and in the proxy, so the 900 s idle limit holds on an open page; two minutes before the limit the page shows an alert with the minutes left and a Stay signed in button (same-origin, no API call, not audited); the page's own clock of activity can only lag the server's, so the warning comes early, never late; the 8-hour absolute limit holds however active
residual: No end-to-end test sees the warning (the real-Keycloak suite was not run); typing alone is not activity, so a clinician typing a long entry without saving is warned and can be signed out; a session ended elsewhere (another tab signs out) is found only at the next request; the warning is checked every 15 s; the in-memory store loses every session on restart; ratings are unreviewed

title: A triage is made with the wrong flowchart or a missed discriminator
hazard: A patient is given a lower urgency than their presentation needs, or is seen late
cause: The wrong presenting-complaint flowchart is picked; a discriminator is skipped or answered from memory; the nurse is interrupted; a discriminator is read as absent when it was not asked
effect: A patient who needs urgent care waits longer than the target; harm from delay
controls: Planned, not built (TR-5, TR-7): a discriminator not asked is stored as not-assessed with a reason and never read as absent, so a missing assessment never lowers the category; the first applicable discriminator sets the suggestion; the nurse confirms or overrides with a reason; every triage is audited and append-only
residual: Nothing is built. No test. Ratings are proposed by the author and unreviewed; likelihood is a guess with no data from any site

title: Children and other groups MTS handles badly are under-triaged
hazard: A child, such as one with congenital heart disease, or a patient whose vital signs are abnormal but not part of the discriminators, is given a low category
cause: Published validation work reports under-triage for some groups, from abstracts only; the discriminators do not use vital signs; the tool is trusted over the patient's look
effect: Delayed assessment of a deteriorating patient
controls: Planned, not built (TR-9, TR-10): latest vitals and NEWS2 or a paediatric score shown beside the category, with a prompt, never an automatic change, when they point to higher urgency; a report of triage category against outcome by group
residual: Nothing is built. The evidence is abstracts only, and the first-edition studies may not transfer to the current edition. Which paediatric score to use is not chosen. Ratings unreviewed

title: A triage category is changed silently or lost
hazard: The category on screen differs from what the nurse confirmed, or a re-categorisation leaves no trace
cause: An update in place; a suggestion saved without confirmation; a pack update that re-scores old triages; a user who overrides with no reason
effect: A clinician acts on the wrong category; no one can tell who changed it
controls: Planned, not built (TR-5): assessments are append-only and nothing updates or deletes one; a change is a new assessment linked to the one it supersedes with a reason and author; a suggestion is never saved without confirmation; each triage stamps its pack version
residual: Nothing is built. Ratings unreviewed

title: A triage pack is stale, mixed or invalid
hazard: A triage runs on a withdrawn or unsupported edition, or two flowchart versions are mixed
cause: The publisher stops supporting earlier editions; a deployer does not update; a pack is edited by hand; an unsigned pack is loaded
effect: Triage on out-of-date discriminators; the record cannot show which rules applied
controls: Planned, not built (TR-6): packs are versioned and an invalid or unsigned pack is refused loudly; each triage stamps its pack version; the update path is documented
residual: Nothing is built. Whether MTS content may be shipped at all is unknown (OQ-T1), so the supply and update route is undefined. Ratings unreviewed

title: A time-target clock fails or floods the board
hazard: A waiting patient passes their target with no signal, or staff learn to ignore the signals
cause: The clock starts at the wrong time; a clock stops with a lost connection; one alert per patient per minute; alert fatigue
effect: A patient waits past the target unseen, or a real breach is ignored
controls: Planned, not built (TR-8): one breach signal per patient, an audit event on a missed target, a test with a fake clock, and the tracking board's behaviour when offline decided with the downtime work
residual: Nothing is built. Downtime behaviour of the clock is not designed. Ratings unreviewed

title: A triage tool is read as an autonomous triager
hazard: Staff or a deployer treats the suggested category as the decision, or the tool is a medical device without its approval
cause: The screen shows the category as a result, not a suggestion; the nurse is under time pressure; an AI or automatic step is added later
effect: Unreviewed automated decisions on who is seen first; regulatory exposure
controls: Planned, not built (TR-7): wording says suggested and the nurse confirms; no automatic triage; the device boundary is reviewed in AS-1 and OQ-6 before any release
residual: Nothing is built. No regulatory advice has been taken. Ratings unreviewed

title: Triage content is used without a licence or is wrongly claimed as MTS
hazard: MTS flowchart text is copied into the repo, or the project is described as MTS-conformant or accredited
cause: The content is licensed through its publisher and the terms for open source are unknown; a contributor pastes a chart
effect: Legal exposure for the project and deployers; clinicians trust a product that has not been checked by the rights holder
controls: Interim policy in plan.md §15.1.1 and spec/triage/index.md §1: no MTS content in the repo, tests or demo data; no claim of accreditation. A CI guard is not built (TR-1)
residual: No guard is in CI, and no one has asked the publisher. Ratings unreviewed

title: A drill or test record is mistaken for, or merged into, a real patient
hazard: A drill or training patient appears in a real list, is offered as a duplicate of a real person, is merged into a real record, or a real patient is created as a drill and hidden
cause: A drill flag is missing or lost on an edit; search or the duplicate check ignores it; a merge does not check it; a screen shows the record without saying it is a drill; the UI banner marks a drill record on the patient page and my-record but nothing else shows the flag (no list label; no tab title; no registration option)
effect: Clinical content for a real person is recorded on a drill record (invisible to ordinary search), or drill content pollutes a real record or a report
controls: Service (EC-10, first slice): `patient_versions.drill`, every version keeps the flag; ordinary search and the duplicate check see real records only, a drill registration is compared only with drill records; a merge between a drill and a real record is refused; the FHIR facade lists real patients only and tags a drill read `urn:epr:record-kind|drill`
residual: The patient banner says DRILL (EC-10) but no other screen does, and the UI cannot register a drill record; nothing stops a person registering a real patient as a drill by mistake; the flag cannot be changed by a later version, so a mistaken one needs a new record; no aggregate or export exists yet to check. Ratings unreviewed

title: A vital sign is recorded, flagged or shown wrongly
hazard: A clinician misses a deteriorating patient, or acts on a wrong measurement
cause: A wrong unit accepted; a value keyed in error that passes the bounds; a flag computed from a range the sender got wrong or did not send; no range read as normal; a measurement attached to the wrong patient; a correction that is not seen; a retracted value still read; a time of day wrong across a clock change
effect: Delayed treatment of deterioration, or treatment on a false reading
controls: Only eight vital signs, one UCUM unit each, no conversion, so a wrong unit is refused 422 with a code; zero and impossible values are refused, and no value needs a stated reason, never zero; the range is the sender's and is never invented, and with no range the flag is null (not assessed), never normal; the flag is computed when read, so a corrected rule cannot leave an old flag behind; append-only versions with a reason, and a mistake is entered-in-error and final; the measured time is stored in UTC with the site's zone beside it and a time more than 5 minutes ahead is refused; clinical-content access: a care relationship (or break-glass), purpose and consent, and a proxy has no scope for observations so is refused; every write is audited in the same transaction and the audit row holds no value, unit or range (2026-10-26); the patient page lists vital signs with a missing value shown with its reason (never 0 or a dash), a value with no range shown as "Not assessed (no range given)" and never as normal, the flag only as words the service computed, the time on the site's clock with UTC beside it, a trend table that lists every standing reading and omits none (2026-10-27), retracted entries collapsed but visible, a every version of an entry can be read (service, 2026-10-26) and from a History button on the page, oldest first, with the reason, author and time, a retracted value still shown (2026-10-27) with the same access decision and an audit row, a mistaken entry is marked entered in error, or corrected as a new version with the earlier kept, from the page with a required reason (2026-10-26), and the form fixes the unit per vital and refuses an empty or unreadable number so nothing is sent as 0 (2026-10-26)
residual: The page is a list, a record form and a per-entry history list only: no comparison of two versions, nothing tells a reader of the old value that it changed, no trend; the history is not tested with a real Keycloak login; the words on the page are English only and no clinician has used or reviewed them; a value keyed wrongly inside the bounds is accepted and shown as recorded; the eight codes and the plausibility bounds are guesses, not clinical limits; a value keyed wrongly inside the bounds is accepted; the sender's range can be wrong, and no table is held to check it; no check that the measurement is of this patient; no second-person check; FHIR Observation is read-only search by patient (2026-10-27; same access decision and audit as the JSON list; an empty result carries a warning that it is not a normal reading; base R4 validator only, no UK Core or US Core profile) and no device feed; a trend table lists every standing reading per vital newest first with a gap shown as its reason, but there is no chart, no NEWS2 (DO-5), and nothing warns of a change over time; a proxy cannot be given observations yet; the 5-minute future limit is a guess; ratings are unreviewed and no clinician has reviewed the rules; the summary page (2026-10-28) shows only the newest reading of each vital, so a clinician who does not open the full record sees no trend and no earlier value, and a newest reading with no value is shown as its reason, never replaced by an older value

title: A patient's request to correct a record is lost, mis-decided or not shown to readers
hazard: A record that is wrong stays wrong, a correction is applied on the wrong authority, or a reader acts on a record that is under dispute without being told
cause: The request is not seen by a clinician in time; a decision is made by the person who asked, or by a role that should not decide; a refusal loses the patient's statement of disagreement; a correction is made by editing instead of a new version; the notice of a pending, amended or refused request is not shown beside the record; the deadlines are wrong; a request or its words leak into the audit trail
effect: A clinician acts on a record the patient has said is wrong, or a patient's correction is silently dropped; a legal right to amend is not honoured
controls: Service (RC-4, 2026-10-27): the rules are pure and tested (`amendment.rs`): the decider is never the requester, every decision needs a non-blank reason, the applied version must be later than the disputed one so the record is corrected by a new version and never edited, nothing leaves a final state, one statement of disagreement is kept unedited; the store is append-only by trigger and every step keeps its event and author; the requester and the decider are the token and never the body; a deciding step needs the clinician role and a withdrawal or statement the patient role, so a patient cannot decide and a clinician cannot speak for the patient; a stale version is 409; the record-level decision applies in full (care relationship, purpose, consent) and a proxy has no scope for amendments so is refused; every write and its audit row are one transaction, and a write whose audit row cannot be written is refused and leaves nothing (audit-failure test); the audit row holds ids, kinds, versions and states, never the request text, a reason or a statement (tested)
residual: The JSON observation list carries the notice and the vitals section shows it (2026-10-27, English wording unreviewed), and the allergy list and its section carry it too (2026-10-27), and so do the FHIR Observation and AllergyIntolerance searches (2026-10-27, as English prose in `note`, accepted by the HL7 validator; not a coded extension, and no read by id or export exists yet); a clinician can decide a request in the UI (2026-10-27) and the request names the record it is about, but nothing checks the version typed; a patient can ask about a vital sign or an allergy from /my-record (2026-10-27, stubbed tests only, not seen with a real login; the clinician page was run once against the real service with login off); the open and overdue count shows only on that patient's page and nothing alerts across patients; a proxy cannot ask; nothing checks that an applied version really corrects the disputed field; only observations and allergies can be amended; who counts as a decider is just the clinician role; the proxy, adult-child and UK/GDPR rectification cases are not modelled; the 60 and 30 days follow HIPAA 164.526 as read by the author and are a guess, as is the grounds list; no clinician or privacy officer has reviewed any of it; not tested with a real Keycloak login; the FHIR notice is coded by an extension at a placeholder address that no consumer is known to read, so a reader that ignores unknown extensions still has only the text (2026-10-28)

title: A hazard is retired while it still applies
hazard: A hazard that still applies is taken off the active list, so the risk it records is no longer managed, watched or shown to the people who decide
cause: The wrong person retires it; evidence is missing, stale, altered or does not show what it claims; the officer who recorded the control also retires it; a retired hazard is not reopened when it is seen again; the register is edited or emptied afterwards; the Clinical Safety Officer role is given to a service account or to everyone
effect: An unsafe feature or workflow stays in use because its hazard looks closed; the safety case reports a risk that has not been controlled
controls: Service (AS-17, 2026-10-28): only the clinical-safety-officer role retires a hazard, and the check does not switch off when login is off, so with no token nobody retires (tested); a retirement without evidence is a 422, each item needs a kind, a reference, a past time and a SHA-256 (tested); whoever recorded a control cannot retire the hazard (tested); any writer reopens with a reason (tested); the register is append-only by trigger and the route has no delete (tested); the role is the token's and never the body's (tested); every step is audited with the evidence hashes and never the free text (tested); the table is in the personal-data inventory (census test)
residual: No clinical safety officer is named (OQ-2), so nobody can retire a hazard yet, and the role has no holder; a hash shows the evidence did not change after it was recorded, not that it is true, and an officer can still attach weak evidence; nothing re-checks evidence later (AS-18); the sign-off for the repository's own hazard log file is still by pull request only (AS-13); a one-person site fails the four-eyes rule; the register is not linked to feature gates (AS-18); the Keycloak role exists but no one holds it; the ratings are the author's proposals

title: A record served as FHIR R5 differs from the stored record
hazard: A partner or clinician reads a version of the record that has lost, changed or reshaped something the stored R4 record says
cause: The R4 to R5 conversion drops or retypes an element (a reaction, a unit, a range, the amendment notice, the 'not recorded' warning) and still answers; a retyped element is mapped wrongly; a search set loses its warning that an empty list is not a statement of none; the answer names the wrong release; the R5 route skips a gate, a consent check or an audit row that its R4 twin has; the partner treats the base R5 shape as a UK Core or US Core profile
effect: A clinician or a partner's system acts on a quieter or different record: an allergy without its reaction, a vital sign without its range, a disputed record shown as undisputed
controls: Service (IO-16, 2026-10-29): R5 is derived from the R4 answer by calling the R4 handler, so the gate, care relationship, purpose, consent and audit row are the R4 ones and there is no second set of converters (route census covers the five new routes); the conversion must report no loss and no warning, so a dropped or retyped element fails the response with a 500 outcome that names no value (tested with a planted field); the one retyping this service's R4 output needs (reaction.manifestation to a concept) is mapped and tested, and any other retyped element still fails; the allergy, observation (value, unit, range, amendment notice) and patient (merge link) bodies the service really writes are converted in tests; the 'not recorded', 'no known allergies' and empty-vitals warnings survive (tested); the HL7 validator accepts each converted body against R5 5.0.0 and refuses a broken one (CI); an Accept naming another release is a 406 and the capability statement says R5, reads only, base R5 with no UK Core or US Core claim (tested); no R5 write route exists
residual: The R4 to R5 differences were not read from the specification (IO-17); only what the converter reports and the validator checks is covered, so a semantic change that keeps the shape would pass; the Accept fhirVersion rule is built for R5 only, not R4; the conversion is by the fhir crate's element tables and one hand-written retyping, neither reviewed by a clinician or by HL7; no real partner has read the output; AuditEvent, Consent and Provenance are not served in R5; the amendment-notice extension URL is a placeholder; ratings are the author's proposals

title: An event leaves the service to a recipient who should not have it
hazard: A change to a patient's record is sent to a subscriber, webhook or other sink that the patient's consent, the recipient's role or the purpose of use does not allow, or is sent twice, or is lost
cause: A producer writes an event without the recipient's roles or purpose, or with the wrong ones; the delivery skips the consent check or the policy check that the read path makes; a consent lookup fails and the delivery goes ahead; the runner delivers an event whose transaction rolled back; a crash after a sink answers delivers again; a sink's error text carries patient data into the attempt table; an event stays pending for ever and nobody sees it
effect: A partner system or a person receives patient data the patient refused or the role may not see; a partner acts on a duplicate or a change that never happened; a change a partner needs never arrives and its copy of the record goes stale
controls: Service (OS-3, 2026-10-30): an event is written in the caller's transaction, so a rollback removes it (tested); before a sink is called the runner makes the read path's own decision for the recipient, policy::evaluate with the recipient's roles and purpose and the patient's consent, and anything but a plain allow is a refusal that is audited, final and never retried (tested for a refusing patient, a role the policy does not allow, and an allow that carries a masking obligation by construction); a failed consent lookup is a failed attempt, never a delivery; a recipient has no care relationship, so a clinical read by a treating role is refused; events and attempts are append-only under database triggers (tested); a retry limit of five with one attempt per run; delivery and refusal are audit rows naming the event, never its content
residual: Nothing calls enqueue and no sink exists (IO-6), so no event leaves the service today and this hazard is about the mechanism, not a live flow; delivery is at least once, so every sink must treat a repeat as a repeat and none is written yet; the roles and purpose are supplied by the producer and are not checked against a registered subscriber list; a sink's error text is stored as given and nothing checks it names no patient data; no alert on events stuck pending or exhausted, no queue-depth metric; backoff exists (30 seconds, doubling) but only its first wait is tested; the claim race between two runners can deliver twice; the loop that runs the runner is not built; no clinician or privacy officer has reviewed the rules

title: A clinician is refused a request by a rate limit while treating a patient
hazard: A request that a clinician needs (a patient search, a record read, a compare at registration) is answered 429 and the screen shows an error or an empty result
cause: The limit is set too low for a busy ward or a shared login; many clinicians share one token subject; a script or a page that polls uses the whole allowance; a restart or a second replica changes who is counted; the UI treats a 429 as no result; an integration under one subject exhausts the allowance of the same subject's interactive use
effect: A clinician cannot see or register a patient for up to a minute, or reads an empty list as none, and delays or alters care
controls: Service (OS-2, 2026-10-30): defaults of 1200 requests and 120 compare calls per minute per subject, far above a person at a screen (a unit test replays five requests a second for ten minutes and a compare every two seconds without a refusal); the answer is 429 with Retry-After and an error body, never an empty list, and the UI proxy passes both on and the shared status check turns a 429 into This one was not carried out and nothing was changed" (UI unit tests); the limit counts only authenticated subjects and fails open when its table is full; a bad setting stops the service starting rather than falling back to a low value; the first refusal in a window is audited and every one is counted in epr_rate_limited_total
evidence: so a rising count is visible"
residual: electronic-patient-record-service-with-rust/src/rate_limit.rs;electronic-patient-record-service-with-rust/tests/http_rate_limit.rs;spec/07-non-functional-requirements.md
status: The Clinical Safety Officer has not answered OQ-OS1 and has not reviewed the defaults; they are a guess at clinical use, not measured on a ward; the limiter ran in a test router, not in the running service; the UI says in words that a 429 was not carried out wherever a page uses the shared status check (24 call sites), but no page was driven to a 429 in a browser test, and a page that handles its own statuses was not audited; a shared login would pool its users into one allowance; no way to lift a limit for one subject without a restart; counts are per replica and lost on restart; an integration and a person under one subject share an allowance

title: A phone number is read under the wrong country's calling code
hazard: A local phone number is turned into an international one with a calling code that is not the site's, so two different people are scored as sharing a phone, or one person's two records are not
cause: A deployment enables the wrong pack, or two packs at once and names the wrong winner; a pack's calling code is wrong; the matcher's default of 44 stays in force where no pack is enabled; the pack was assembled from a public source and no person who works with that country's standards has checked it; a changed pack changes who is linked to whom without a replay
effect: A shared phone raises a pair's similarity toward Review or a link, or a real match is missed, so a clinician sees, or writes to, the wrong person's record or a split record
controls: Service and packs (OS-10, 2026-10-30): the calling code comes only from an enabled pack that loads; a pack with an unknown key, a code outside 1 to 999, a mismatched id, no vectors, or a vector the real matcher does not satisfy does not load and the service does not start; two enabled packs that disagree stop startup unless the deployer names the winner; with no pack enabled the matcher's own default applies, so behaviour is unchanged; a phone is never more than half the household evidence and a phone alone cannot auto-link (matcher controls under H-001); the rules have a SHA-256 logged at start; every shipped pack says reviewed none and a warning is logged for each enabled pack
residual: No person who works with either country's standards has reviewed a pack; the calling codes were taken from the E.164 list and not checked against a second source; the matcher's default of 44 means an empty list is the UK, not neutral, which misreads an Australian number at a deployment that forgets to enable au; the hash is logged but not written on records or link decisions, so a record does not say which rules applied; no dry run over a labelled corpus before a pack change; the pack was never enabled in a running service; only the phone code is a pack, every other country assumption in the equity audit remains in code
